question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ -1 & -3 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-22 \\ 11 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ shown above. If the general solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of  $a+\frac{b}{c}?$
question.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{1}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {1}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 6 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ -1 & -3 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 6 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-22 \\ 11 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 6 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ -4 & -12 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 6 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-22 \\ 44 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}9 & 27 \\ 27 & 81\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-81 \\ -243\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}9 & 27 & -81 \\ 27 & 81 & -243\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 27 & -81 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=-9-3{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-9-3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+\frac{b}{c}=-9+\frac{(-3)}{1}=-12.
$$
